parsed.explanation: Combined national and state regime imposes universal facility exclusion in government buildings including airports, with criminal trespass for refusal; national entry screening flags document/sex discrepancies and can lead to refusal or lifetime fraud finding; immigration custody and prison policies document severe harm. Protections exist—national hate-crime statute, court injunctions, local anti-discrimination, private businesses outside the state facility law—but no visitor-facing remedy is shown to work. Not execution or organized targeting of trans visitors, but high risk on discovery.

entry_documents.exposure: National visa/border cable treats sex-document discrepancy as reason to refuse or request more evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation can support lifetime fraud ineligibility. Foreign passports with X or mismatched markers may trigger secondary screening. State driver's licence/birth-certificate rules block marker changes.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker national passports remain valid until expiry; passport policy is in litigation; legal-aid FAQ exists. No documented visitor-facing protection against border refusal or fraud finding.
entry_documents.interaction: A mismatch at visa/entry can move to secondary inspection, refusal, or detention; state document rules signal friction but foreign visitors carry home passports.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men; national prison policies impose conversion-therapy-like regimes, denial of care. Facility refusal can lead to criminal trespass charge; border fraud suspicion can lead to detention.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: One bathroom prosecution was dismissed on standing; some executive orders enjoined; national hate-crime statute covers GI. No documented effective remedy for immigration detention or custody abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border discrepancy can become fraud investigation and custody; a facility refusal can become misdemeanor prosecution. Both interact with national and state enforcement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State statute bars trans use of restrooms/changing rooms matching identity in government-owned/leased buildings incl airports, courthouses, schools, prisons, parks, beaches; authority figure may order departure; refusal is criminal trespass. National order bars government-funded congruent facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private businesses are outside the state statute; some local protections exist; one arrest was dismissed; national courts blocked some orders. No visitor remedy shown to reverse exclusion.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Airport and public-building facilities are the sharpest daily exposure; state law adds to national facility restrictions.

care_services.exposure: State restricts adult gender-affirming care (waiting period, insurance bar, physician-only) and bans minors; national orders frame minor care as mutilation and propose public-insurance bar under 18; hospitals subpoenaed for under-19 records.
care_services.protection: Court injunctions and a permanent block on some care bans; emergency care not documented; no visitor-specific care protection.
care_services.interaction: A trans visitor needing routine or emergency care may face refusal, delay, or record exposure; minors face outright care bans.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy lists 'radically pro-transgender' violent groups; justice reward memo cites 'radical gender ideology'; executive orders target teachers/schools facilitating social transition. State hate-crime law lacks GI coverage.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers GI; some local anti-discrimination laws; courts enjoined some orders. Enforcement for visitors not documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing raises official suspicion and can color police/border responses; state lacks GI hate-crime recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans puberty blockers/hormones/surgery for minors and says social transition is not treatment; national orders threaten prosecution of teachers using preferred names/pronouns and subpoena under-19 records; custody-modification laws target families.
minors_guardians.protection: Court injunctions block some care bans; no visitor-specific protection for travelling minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces care denial and potential official inquiry; border document checks add exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Travel advisory warns of health/safety/freedom risks; state recorded 3.7 trans women murders per 100k/year and 'Do Not Travel' label; state hate-crime law lacks GI; no state GI anti-discrimination. Rate lacks background comparison.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers GI; local city/county protections; one bathroom prosecution dismissed. No evidence of organized targeting of trans visitors.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police may enforce facility law and lack GI hate-crime coverage; national statute offers theoretical recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Facility statute never substantively tested; passport policy and care litigation unresolved; travel advisories not reissued/withdrawn. Visitor remedies for border refusal or facility exclusion are not shown to work.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts enjoined some orders, dismissed one bathroom case, legal-aid FAQ; national hate-crime statute. Local protections exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved legal status means exposure varies by stage and official discretion; no reliable pre-travel remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.25-A documents weekly police raids, extortion and repeat detention; our dossier lacks that street-level pattern but adds statewide public-facility exclusion reaching airports and national border/immigration-custody harms. Similar high-risk tier, with broader universal exposure and somewhat less documented police extortion; rating slightly above 0.25.

0.55-B has extended secondary screening and refusal but no facility ban or criminal trespass; our case adds statewide facility exclusion, possible misdemeanor, and severe immigration-custody harms. That makes it materially lower than 0.55-B.
0.75-C has trained border officers, tribunal remedies and low detention severity; our case has document-mismatch screening, facility exclusion and no working visitor remedy. Much lower than 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a layered exposure: national passport/visa rules and border screening create discovery risk; the state facility statute turns restroom use in public buildings into exclusion with possible misdemeanor; custody and immigration detention carry documented abuse. Protections are partial and contested: courts have blocked some care bans and dismissed one bathroom case on standing, and national hate-crime law covers GI, but the state lacks GI anti-discrimination and hate-crime coverage, and no visitor remedy is shown to reverse facility exclusion or border refusal. The result is high risk if outed, though not the extreme of automatic imprisonment or execution. Private businesses fall outside the state facility law, but public buildings, airports, and border/custody stages dominate the visitor experience.
